_note: **The second surveyable map, and the first that reads a compass badly.** `survey::mods_for` has taken a `map` argument since M11.6 and never read it — its own doc says why: *a second surveyable map is meant to be a data drop plus an arm here, and a signature that could not tell two maps apart would have to change to become one that could.* This is that data drop. There is iron under the sand, so the needle is no use and the paper survey is: on the Reach a compass quiets the ground and an atlas is loud, and here it is the other way round. That is the whole point of a second one — it makes *which instrument you built* a question about where you are going rather than a question with one answer. The door states the trade before you walk through it, in core's own numbers, because `kit_reading_json` runs `mods_for` against the map on the far side.

places.name: the way back off the sands
prose: Up the shingle and onto ground that stays where it is.

places.name: the way under the flat
places.shut: The flat goes out past the low water for four hundred paces and then stops being flat. There is iron under it and it moves; without something to read it with you would be walking on a guess.
prose: The crust gives under the heel of your hand and keeps giving, and what is under it is not sand.
Somebody has cut steps. They are cut for going down and not for coming back, which is a thing you can tell by looking at them.

places.name: the cart, in the lee of the north bank
prose: A cart with a canvas over it and no wheel marks behind it, which on a flat this size is the first thing you notice.
Somebody very large is sitting on the tailgate with their back to the goods, and they do not get up when you arrive.

places.name: the cart, at the eastern edge of the silt
prose: The canvas is off and there are five things laid out on sacking, each one in its own square of it.
The person on the tailgate has not looked at them once. They are looking at you.

places.name: the cart, by the western rock
prose: Parked where the rock throws a shadow, which is the only shade on the flat and is about four feet of it.
A ledger is open on the boards with nothing written in it. The large person's hand is flat on the page.

places.name: the cart, where the iron reads strongest
prose: Every needle you own is pointing at the ground here, so the cart is either very well placed or not placed at all.
Whoever is on the tailgate has the look of somebody who has been asked to move on and has not.

places.name: the cart, on the southern silt
prose: Tracks come to the cart from the north and none leave it, and there are a great many of them.
The five things on the sacking are the same five things. They are always the same five things.

places.name: the cart, near the tenth survey
prose: Close enough to the folding table that you could shout between them, and nobody ever has.
The person on the tailgate stands up as you come in, which is the first time they have done that.
